title: Butter chicken
steps: Mix the chicken with all the marinade ingredients and leave for at least 1 hour, or overnight in the fridge.
Cook the chicken in a hot, lightly oiled pan or under a very hot grill for 8 to 10 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges. It does not need to be cooked through.
Melt half the butter in a wide pan. Add the tomatoes with a pinch of salt and cook for about 15 minutes until soft and jammy.
Blend the tomatoes until smooth and return the sauce to the pan.
Add the chicken and a splash of water if the sauce is thick. Simmer for 10 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Stir in the cream, crushed kasuri methi, sugar if using, and the remaining butter. Warm through for 2 minutes and adjust the salt.
Serve with naan or basmati rice.
notes: Use a small amount of chilli powder for mild heat; kashmiri chilli adds colour more than heat.

title: Masala dosa with potato filling
steps: Soak the rice, and separately the urad dal with the fenugreek seeds, in plenty of water for 5 to 6 hours.
Grind the dal to a fluffy, light batter, adding cold water a little at a time. Grind the rice more coarsely. Combine, add salt and mix well with your hand.
Cover and leave in a warm place for 8 to 12 hours until bubbly and slightly sour. The batter should roughly double.
For the filling, heat 2 tbsp oil. Add the mustard seeds, and when they pop add the curry leaves, chilli and onion. Cook until soft.
Add the turmeric, potatoes, salt and a splash of water. Mix and cook for 5 minutes, then keep warm.
Heat a flat non-stick or cast-iron pan until hot. Pour a ladle of batter into the centre and spiral it outward into a thin circle. Drizzle a little oil around the edge.
Cook until the underside is deep golden and the top is dry. Spoon the filling along the centre, fold and serve at once with coconut chutney and sambar.
notes: The first dosa usually tears. Wipe the pan with half an onion between dosas to stop sticking.

title: Hilsa in mustard sauce

ingredients.note: black or yellow, soaked in warm water 15 minutes and ground with 2 green chillies and a pinch of salt

steps: Rub the fish with salt and half the turmeric and set aside for 10 minutes.
Grind the soaked mustard seeds with 2 green chillies and a pinch of salt to a smooth paste. Avoid over-grinding, which makes the paste bitter. Mix it with 150 ml cold water.
Heat the mustard oil until it just starts to smoke, then lower the heat. Add the fish and fry lightly for 1 to 2 minutes per side without browning.
Pour the mustard mixture over the fish, add the slit chillies and the remaining turmeric, and cover.
Cook gently for 8 to 10 minutes, shaking the pan rather than stirring so the fish stays intact.
Finish with a drizzle of raw mustard oil and serve with plain steamed rice.
notes: Hilsa has many fine bones. Frozen hilsa is available at South Asian grocers. Rohu or another oily fish can stand in.

title: Instant khaman dhokla
steps: Grease a 20 cm round tin and set up a steamer with boiling water.
Whisk the besan, yogurt, sugar, ginger, chilli, turmeric, lemon juice and salt with about 200 ml water into a smooth, pourable batter. Rest for 10 minutes.
Stir in the baking soda just before steaming. The batter will foam up.
Pour into the tin and steam, covered, for 15 to 18 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Heat the oil, add the mustard seeds and curry leaves, and when they crackle pour in the sugar water and bring to a boil.
Cut the dhokla into squares, spoon the tempering over the top and leave 5 minutes to absorb. Serve with green chutney.

title: Gulab jamun with milk powder
steps: Boil the sugar, water and cardamom for 5 to 6 minutes until lightly sticky. Add the rose water and keep the syrup warm.
Mix the milk powder, flour and baking soda. Rub in the melted ghee, then add the warm milk a spoonful at a time to make a soft, smooth dough. Do not knead hard.
Rest the dough for 10 minutes, then roll into about 16 smooth, crack-free balls. They will double in size.
Heat the frying fat to a low medium heat, about 130 to 140 C. Fry the balls in batches, turning constantly, for 8 to 10 minutes until deep golden brown all over.
Lift out, drain briefly and drop into the warm syrup.
Soak for at least 2 hours so they swell and absorb the syrup. Serve warm.
notes: If the fat is too hot the outside browns while the centre stays raw. Cracks in the balls mean the dough was too dry.

title: Mumbai-style vada pav
steps: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a pan, crackle the mustard seeds, then add the curry leaves, green chilli, ginger and garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the turmeric and the mashed potato with salt. Cook for 3 minutes, then add the coriander and lemon juice. Cool and shape into 8 small balls.
For the dry chutney, grind the coconut, garlic, chilli powder, peanuts and a pinch of salt to a coarse powder.
Whisk the batter ingredients with the water to a smooth, thick coating consistency, adding salt to taste. Rest for 10 minutes.
Heat the frying oil to about 175 C. Dip each potato ball in batter and fry for 4 to 5 minutes until golden, turning often. Drain.
Toast the pav lightly on a dry pan. Spread the inside with the chutney, put in a vada, press lightly and serve hot.
notes: The dry chutney contains peanuts; leave them out for a nut-free version. Add a fried green chilli on the side for more heat.

title: Kerala-style fish curry

ingredients.note: steaks or thick fillets, cut in chunks
soaked in 100 ml hot water, strained
grated, ground to paste with a little water (optional for richer curry)

steps: Mix the chilli powder and turmeric with 3 tbsp of water to make a paste.
Heat the oil in a clay pot or wide pan. Add the mustard seeds and fenugreek and let the mustard pop, then add half the curry leaves.
Add the onion, ginger, garlic and green chilli and cook for 5 to 6 minutes until softened.
Add the spice paste and cook for 2 minutes, stirring, until it smells cooked and the oil starts to separate.
Pour in the tamarind water and the 250 ml water with salt. Bring to a simmer for 5 minutes. Stir in the coconut paste if using.
Add the fish, spoon the gravy over it and simmer very gently for 8 to 10 minutes without stirring, shaking the pot instead, until the fish is just cooked.
Add the remaining curry leaves and rest for at least 15 minutes. Serve with rice.
notes: Kodampuli can replace tamarind: soak 3 to 4 pieces. Without the coconut paste the curry is thinner and tangier, as in many home kitchens.

title: Dal baati churma
steps: Rub 100 g ghee into the flour, semolina, soda and salt until like breadcrumbs. Add the yogurt and enough water to make a firm dough. Rest for 20 minutes.
Boil the two dals in the water with turmeric for 30 to 35 minutes until very soft, mashing lightly. Add salt.
Heat the oven to 200 C. Shape the dough into 8 tight balls, press a dent into each, and bake for 30 to 35 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and cracks appear.
Dip the hot baati briefly in melted ghee. Set 3 aside for the churma.
For the churma, crush the 3 baati to coarse crumbs. Stir over low heat with 3 tbsp ghee, jaggery and cardamom for 3 minutes until the jaggery melts in.
Heat 2 tbsp ghee, fry the cumin, asafoetida, garlic and dried chillies until fragrant, then add the chilli powder and pour the sizzling mixture over the dal. Top with coriander.
Serve the crumbled baati with the dal, and the churma on the side.
notes: Traditional baati are baked over embers; an oven gives a good home result. The dish contains ghee and dairy.

title: Hyderabadi dum biryani
steps: Fry the onions in the oil over medium heat for 20 to 25 minutes until deep golden brown and crisp. Lift out and drain, reserving the oil.
Mix the lamb with all marinade ingredients, half the fried onions and 3 tbsp of the onion oil. Marinate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Boil the 3 l water with the whole spices, bay leaves and a generous amount of salt. Add the soaked rice and boil for 5 to 6 minutes until about 70 percent cooked. Drain.
Spread the lamb in a heavy pot. Layer the rice over it, then top with the remaining fried onions, ghee, saffron milk and a little mint.
Seal the pot with foil or dough and a tight lid. Cook on high for 5 minutes, then reduce to the lowest heat for 45 to 50 minutes.
Rest for 10 minutes unopened, then fold the rice gently from the bottom so that the meat and rice mix. Serve with raita.
notes: Chicken thighs can replace lamb: marinate 2 hours and cook the dum for 30 minutes. Make sure the lamb is tender before serving.

title: Kashmiri-style rogan josh

ingredients.note: bone-in shoulder or leg, in chunks

steps: Heat the mustard oil until it smokes lightly and turns pale, then reduce the heat. Add the cloves, cardamom, cinnamon and bay leaves.
Add the lamb and fry over high heat for 8 to 10 minutes until browned.
Lower the heat. Mix the chilli powder with 3 tbsp water and stir it in with the asafoetida and a good pinch of salt. Cook for 2 minutes.
Take the pot off the heat for a minute, then add the yogurt a spoonful at a time, stirring constantly so that it does not split. Return to the heat and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the ground fennel and ginger, then the hot water. Cover and simmer for 60 to 75 minutes until the lamb is tender and the oil floats on top.
Stir in the garam masala, adjust the salt and rest for 10 minutes. Serve with rice.
notes: Use less chilli powder for a milder dish; the colour comes from Kashmiri chilli, which is mild. Skip the black cardamom if you cannot find it.
